speaker: (the stallman)
text: Second book, sir, if you are still standing in it. Two shillings.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have stood in it four times since March. Today I am reading the second book standing, and I am buying it. Two shillings.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is the dearest book since Golding.

speaker: john_harrison
text: You may read it, Master Shakespeare, but you may not wear it out.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I will carry it, and the oak can rest. The two shillings are for him.

speaker: (the stallman)
text: Two shillings. The book is yours. I am not wrapping a quarrel.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Sam's kings. You'll not find a laugh in four books, Will.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Michael. I was not looking for a laugh. The cousin is the same cousin, and the stanza is smooth.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Buy the Daniel. Then come and tell me why mine's better.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have bought his kings. I have not bought a quarrel with you.

speaker: john_harrison
text: Two shillings is the whole of my interest, and it is already leaving my neighbour's board. Good day.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Five minutes, Will. Home, and the trade. Arden. You say it as we do. Half London thinks it's a lady's name.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Arden is a wood. I am not correcting London today. I was down there this Lent. I am not sending anything else out of this yard.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Fourteen lines, Will, and I have sixty sonnets. How many have you?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You will not have the number. I am careful with it. So are you, which is why we are still talking.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Careful is the Warwickshire way of wanting the same chair. I do not ask you to envy Sam. Admit the stanza is smooth, and we can be done.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is smooth. I do not envy him. A smooth king is a king I can read. It is not a king I have to answer this afternoon.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Sonnets are a trade. We both know the length. We do not have to count each other's stock in a churchyard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No count. Five minutes is enough home for a Tuesday. I am taking the book.

speaker: (the stallman)
text: Mind the cloister if it drips. I have sold it once.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Come back when you have a reason mine is worse. I shall be at a board. I am usually at a board.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will come when I have read him against the chronicle, not against you.

speaker: john_harrison
text: Against the chronicle is your chamber. Against this board, you are finished.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Do not let four books with no laugh make you grave all the way to Bishopsgate. Four books is still only four books.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Four books. Two shillings. I can carry both. I am going before I start the third book on one foot.

speaker: michael_drayton
text: Go, then. Give you good day, Will.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Good day, Michael.
